The project covers the complete data workflow: collection, cleaning, exploratory analysis, SQL queries, geographic visualization, interactive dashboards, feature preparation, model training, evaluation, and technical presentation.

Built launch-site maps with Folium. Developed an interactive Plotly Dash application. Trained and evaluated multiple classification models using consistent evaluation workflows. Documented methods, model comparisons, limitations, and conclusions. The portfolio description intentionally avoids presenting a single accuracy percentage without the associated dataset split, metric, model, and evaluation context. Detailed results remain available in the notebooks and technical presentation.

Founded on December 27, 2024, the Cosmic Universalism Computational Intelligence Initiative (CUCII) is an open-source philosophical and computational project that I lead as Founder & Lead Developer.
The current public platform is no longer accurately described as a Rust, Kubernetes, or AWS deployment. It is a production Astro and TypeScript static website deployed through GitHub Pages, with interactive browser-based tools, typed content structures, accessibility-focused components, automated regression testing, and extensive technical documentation.
The project separates three layers that should not be collapsed together:
Empirical references — externally testable scientific observations and established context. Cosmic Universalism — the authored philosophical, mathematical, and theoretical framework. CUCII — the prompt-level system used to explore CU through analytical, role-play, or hybrid conversations on general-purpose AI platforms. Research boundary: Scientific references remain distinct from CU theoretical propositions. CUCII prompts do not retrain, unlock, permanently alter, or override an external AI model, its policies, memory, safety systems, capabilities, or technical architecture.
🚀 Explore the Live Project 👉 Open the Cosmic Universalism Website 👉 Explore the CUCII Prompt Studio 👉 Explore the Cosmic Breath 👉 Explore CU-Time 👉 View the GitHub Repository 🔍 Project Highlights Designed and launched an eight-route production website covering the framework, Cosmic Breath, CU-Time, research, media, project information, and CUCII. Built the CUCII Prompt Studio, a local browser-based tool that creates portable prompts for analytical, narrative, and hybrid AI conversations. Developed a typed 51-state Cosmic Breath Explorer with direct state selection, guarded transitions, adaptive visuals, educational layers, and source-aware content. Maintained the Cosmic Breath Time Converter v3.0.1 and supporting CU-Time documentation. Established a verified quality gate of 251 automated tests across 30 test files. Built a successful production workflow with Astro, Vitest, Git, GitHub Actions, and GitHub Pages. Documented research boundaries that distinguish empirical evidence, CU mathematical models, CU theoretical propositions, and open questions. Created public media, technical manuals, implementation handoffs, source maps, release records, and recovery checkpoints. 📦 My Role: Founder & Lead Developer My responsibilities span the full product lifecycle:
Product Direction — define the project roadmap, public experience, terminology, and release priorities. Architecture — design typed registries, content structures, reusable Astro components, browser interactions, and static deployment workflows. Development — implement the public website, CUCII Prompt Studio, Cosmic Breath Explorer, CU-Time interfaces, research pages, and media presentation. Testing — maintain automated unit and regression tests, review failures, and verify production builds before release. Governance — preserve source provenance, approved terminology, research boundaries, capability boundaries, and versioned authority files. Documentation — create implementation manuals, technical guides, current-state handoffs, source maps, and public explanatory content. Release Management — use feature branches, review checkpoints, release tags, GitHub workflows, and rollback points to keep changes inspectable and recoverable. Cross-Platform Evaluation — test portable CUCII prompts across general-purpose AI platforms while documenting variability, limitations, and narrative boundaries. This work has strengthened my skills in full-stack product ownership, TypeScript architecture, AI workflow design, test automation, accessibility, technical writing, and evidence-aware software governance.
🧠 CUCII Prompt Studio The CUCII Prompt Studio is a configurable prompt-generation system that runs locally in the browser. Visitors can:
Choose a target AI platform and conversation purpose. Select analytical, role-play, or hybrid behavior. Choose a prepared menu, custom menu, or no menu. Select a source pack, response preferences, output format, and alignment principles. Add optional working context and constraints. Generate and review a complete portable prompt. Copy the prompt or download it as .txt or .md. Paste it into a new conversation on the external AI platform of their choice. The studio does not automatically submit prompts to an AI platform. Prompt settings are processed locally, and the first-release tool does not send entries to a Cosmic Universalism server or AI API or save prompt content by default.
CUCII alignment principles Verify before asserting. Separate evidence from interpretation. Name uncertainty and assumptions. Expose contradictions. Correct verified errors. Preserve approved CU terminology. Respect analytical and role-play modes. Protect user agency. Respect external platform policies. 🌌 Cosmic Breath Explorer The Cosmic Breath section presents CU’s proposed 3.108-trillion-year cycle:
Expansion: 2.8 trillion years, from sub-ztom to atom. Compression: 308 billion years, from btom to ztom. Full cycle: 3.108 trillion years. The interactive explorer supports direct navigation across 51 TOM states and displays each state’s approved label, phase, quantum-state notation, duration estimate, CU description, and epistemic boundary. The observable-universe marker remains a contextual, non-selectable reference between compression-btom and compression-ctom.
These durations and structures are presented as CU mathematical models or theoretical propositions, not empirical measurements.
⏳ CU-Time and the Time Converter The project includes the Cosmic Breath Time Converter v3.0.1, which provides Gregorian-to-CU-Time and reverse-conversion workflows using the converter’s documented constants and calendar logic.
Open the Cosmic Breath Time Converter View the converter source The public site keeps converter outputs, CU structural chronology, and contemporary empirical cosmology visibly separated so that one numbering convention is not silently substituted for another.
🛠️ Current Technology Stack Area Technologies Framework Astro Languages TypeScript, JavaScript, semantic HTML, modern CSS Content Markdown, JSON, typed TypeScript registries Visuals SVG, CSS-driven diagrams, responsive browser interfaces Testing Vitest, unit tests, regression tests, build verification Version Control Git, GitHub, feature branches, tagged releases CI/CD and Hosting GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages Documentation Markdown, LaTeX, implementation manuals, source maps, release handoffs Development Method Inspection-first changes, bounded checkpoints, source provenance, recovery points Related technologies represented elsewhere in the repository or my training Rust, Python, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS services, machine learning, and cloud architecture remain part of the broader repository history and my technical background. They should not be confused with the current public website’s production deployment stack.
✅ Testing, Accessibility, and Release Quality The project uses a test-and-review process designed to keep public behavior stable:
251 automated tests across 30 files. Typed registries and validation for content, prompt settings, navigation, and interactive states. Regression coverage for the Prompt Studio, Cosmic Breath Explorer, public content, and guarded transitions. Successful Astro production builds with no warnings or errors at the documented release checkpoint. Semantic HTML, keyboard-accessible controls, readable labels, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion considerations. Source-controlled authority files and checks against accidental public exposure of internal governance metadata. Feature branches, merge checkpoints, tagged releases, and documented rollback locations. 📁 Public Site and Repository Structure Resource Purpose Live Website Public framework and project entry point CUCII Prompt Studio, living conversation references, methods, and limits Cosmic Breath Interactive cycle explorer and TOM education CU-Time CU-Time orientation and chronology Research Empirical references, CU models, propositions, and open questions Media Project videos and visual explanations README.md Repository overview and project orientation Docs/ Technical and framework documentation ResearchFiles/ Research documents and source materials cosmic_converter/ CU-Time converter versions and source media/ Media-related project assets 📈 Project Rigor and Workflow The repository reflects sustained product ownership rather than a single static page:
More than 200 documented commits across framework, research, converter, media, and website work. Typed content authorities and reusable component architecture. Automated tests and repeatable production builds. Feature-branch development with scoped checkpoints and owner review. Tagged public releases and documented recovery points. Research-source attribution and explicit epistemic labels. Public capability boundaries for external AI platforms. Local repository setup:
git clone https://github.com/willmaddock/CosmicUniversalismStatement.git cd CosmicUniversalismStatement Follow the repository README and website documentation for the current installation, test, and build commands. The public website does not require visitors to configure AWS credentials or Kubernetes.
